chapter: Looking back: rock, blues, childhood and guitar innovators
title: Records and minstrel shows in Montgomery
summary: His mother's records of Armstrong, Bessie Smith and the classics, and the touring minstrel shows with good bands, were his music in a small town.

bands.name: Red Nichols and His Five Pennies

story.theme_name: Growing up and learning music: family, first instruments, teachers
story.community_name: Growing up with radio, records and family listening

blocks.x: I heard everything -- I heard all kinds of music. My mother would have records of Louie Armstrong and Nichols his band, she would have records of Red Nichols and his band. She would have records of the blues, whoever was playing the blues she would have the blues singers. Bessie Smith, whatever. She would have the classics, you know, records of concerts, classics. I was exposed to it all, you know.
All on recordings, no, Yeah, all on records.

Yeah, well -- and in a small town, actually we didn't hear too much live music unless it was a minstrel show or you would hear some good music there. You know you never knew anything about Rubin and Jerry and --
Tell me about Rubin and Jerry.
Rubin and Jerry was like a minstrel show, and they would --
Well, okay, they'd come to town and pitch a tent, and they have the comedians and the singers and the band, and it's Mr. Bones, and you know, the minstrel show. Have you never seen a minstrel show?
Oh, how about that. Well, this is quite interesting. They would have, as I said, always a good band with singers, and they would tell the corny jokes and the black face comedians, you know.
They were black, they were black, yeah.
And -- but the blacks were the comedians --
Yeah, and they would put the white around their lips, and you know, the white -- it was very, you know -- sure. And --

They would play current tunes, you know, whatever the current tunes were, and they were good musicians, you know. Played Dixieland or whatever it -- you know, whatever. And they were good bands. So that was about the extent of it. You didn't have too many touring bands in our town, you know. I was in Montgomery. It was practically a --
